content: This medication is contraindicated during pregnancy. If you become pregnant or suspect you might be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. This medication may reduce breast milk production. A small amount of the drug can pass into breast milk and may have adverse effects on a nursing infant. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain drugs may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control by decreasing the levels of birth control hormones in your body, potentially leading to pregnancy. Examples include griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins (such as rifampin, rifabutin), ritonavir, and St. John’s Wort. Inform your doctor when starting any new medication and discuss whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods. This medication may interfere with specific laboratory tests, such as blood tests for clotting factors or thyroid function, potentially causing inaccurate results. In the event of an overdose with severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While taking this medication, regular comprehensive physical exams, including laboratory and medical tests (e.g., blood pressure, breast exams, pelvic exams, Pap smears), should be conducted. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, the advice may vary depending on the brand and the number of doses missed. Refer to the product package information for specific instructions. You may need to use backup birth control methods, such as condoms or spermicides, to prevent pregnancy. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, headache, abdominal cramps or bloating, breast tenderness, swelling of the ankles or feet (fluid retention), or weight changes. Vaginal bleeding between periods (spotting) or missed/irregular periods may occur, especially during the first few months of use. If any of these effects persist or worsen, inform your doctor or pharmacist promptly. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. However, it may increase your blood pressure and, in rare cases, cause serious (sometimes fatal) complications from blood clots, such as heart attack, stroke, or clots in the lungs or legs. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you have diabetes, this medication may affect your blood sugar levels. Monitor your blood sugar regularly as directed and share the results with your doctor. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination. Inform your doctor if you have recently undergone or will undergo surgery, or if you will be confined to a bed or chair for an extended period (e.g., during a long plane flight), as these conditions increase the risk of blood clots, especially when using hormonal birth control. This medication may cause blotchy, dark areas on your face and skin (melasma). Sunlight can worsen this effect. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may develop vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses. It may take longer to conceive after stopping birth control pills. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. If you become pregnant or suspect pregnancy, inform your doctor immediately.
